title: Dangerous Waystone Modifiers: Reroll, Run or Skip (PoE 2 0.5)
summary: How to read Path of Exile 2 Waystone modifiers in 0.5: which map mods are dangerous for your build, how revives scale with modifier count, and when to reroll, run, sell or skip a map.
description: A decision-first guide to dangerous PoE 2 Waystone modifiers: read the mod line, a modifier danger matrix, a build-profile diagnostic, a risk-reward matrix, reroll/run/sell/skip rules, a before-opening checklist, and a death diagnostic.
prerequisites: Access to the Atlas map device and a stock of Waystones
A build whose defences and damage you understand well enough to spot bad mods
author: Exile2 Guides Editorial Team
imageAlt: A stack of Waystones, the map-opening items in Path of Exile 2 endgame

items.title: How do modifiers affect reward and danger?
body: Every modifier added to a Waystone raises both rewards and danger. More modifiers also reduce the number of revives you get when you open the map.

items.title: How many revives do I get?
body: As a rule of thumb: a Normal (0-mod) Waystone gives the most revives, a Magic (2-mod) fewer, a Rare 4-mod fewer still, and a Rare 6-mod or Corrupted map gives zero - one death ends the run. Exact counts should be re-confirmed on the client.

items.title: Which mods are dangerous for everyone?
body: No Regeneration / Reduced Recovery, reflecting or elemental-avoidance mods, chaos ground, and Corrupted 6-modifier maps (zero revives) are dangerous regardless of build. Build-specific mods matter too - see the matrix.

items.title: When should I skip a map?
body: Skip any map whose combined mods your build cannot survive, especially zero-revive corrupted maps, until your character consistently clears T15 content.

sections.title: How to read a Waystone
paragraphs: A Waystone opens an Atlas map and sets its modifiers. Prefixes and suffixes both raise monster difficulty and improve rewards, so the line is a trade-off, not a free bonus.

Revives are the safety budget. The more modifiers a Waystone carries, the fewer retry attempts you get - and a heavily modified or corrupted map can offer none at all. Always check the revive count on the map device before you open.
bullets: Modifier count drives both loot and danger - more is not automatically better.
Corrupted and 6-modifier maps commonly grant zero revives; one death loses the map and everything inside.
Tablets add region-wide bonuses; Magic maps unlock 1 slot, Rare 2, 6-mod 3.
Active map modifiers are shown in the top-right of the minimap while you are inside.

sections.title: Modifier danger matrix
sections.intro: Rate each mod against your own build. Exact modifier text and rolls should be re-confirmed on the live 0.5.4 client.

modifiers.symptom: Your flasks and skills no longer heal you; chip damage becomes lethal.
modifiers.action: Skip on low-recovery builds; add life-on-hit or leech before running.

modifiers.symptom: Your main damage is resisted or reflected back at you.
modifiers.action: Check your resistances; avoid reflect maps entirely if you cannot mitigate.

modifiers.symptom: Telegraphed volleys are harder to dodge.
modifiers.action: Use cover and only run if your build is mobile.

modifiers.symptom: Monsters close gaps and surround you.
modifiers.action: Bring movement or escape tools before running.
Never run on a leech-only build.
Compensate with resistances and layered defence.

modifiers.symptom: Continuous chaos damage bypasses most defences.
modifiers.action: Cap chaos resistance before T15+ corrupted maps.

modifiers.symptom: One death ends the map with no retry.
modifiers.action: Only when you consistently survive T15 content.

sections.title: Build-profile forbidden mods
sections.intro: Pick your build archetype to see which modifiers should be red flags for you.

rules.title: Melee red flags
steps: Extra / Faster Projectiles and Increased Monster Speed make melee positioning brutal.
No Regeneration still hurts, but leech-on-hit usually covers it.
Avoid maps that combine speed + projectiles until your defences are solid.

rules.title: Caster / elemental red flags
steps: Reflect and elemental-avoidance mods directly cut your damage.
Monsters that avoid your damage type are a hard skip if you cannot swap.
No Regeneration is manageable if you have flask sustain.

rules.title: Summoner red flags
steps: Map-wide monster speed and teleport can overwhelm your minions' positioning.
Reflect is rarely an issue for minion damage, but check aura reservation mods.
Chaos ground still punishes low chaos resist.

rules.title: Leech-dependent red flags
steps: No Life / Mana Leech removes your only sustain - a hard skip.
No Regeneration compounds the problem.
Run these maps only with a flask or life-on-hit backup.

defaultResult.title: General forbidden-mod list
steps: Treat No Regeneration, No Leech, reflect and zero-revive corrupted maps as red for most builds.
Build a personal forbidden-mod list based on your defences.
Re-check it whenever you swap a core item or support.

sections.title: Risk versus reward
sections.intro: Decide whether a juiced map is worth opening.

rows.choice: Normal or Magic Waystone for progression
rows.reward: Steady map completion and Atlas points

rows.risk: Zero revives - one death loses everything
rows.reward: Highest tier rolls and T16 chance

rows.choice: Running a mod your build cannot survive

sections.title: Reroll, run, sell or skip
paragraphs: Do not treat every map as a must-run. Match the map to your build's current strength.
bullets: Reroll: use an Orb of Alchemy / Chaos / Vaal to change modifiers only if the result is clearly safer or more rewarding for your build.
Run: open Normal/Magic for progression, and Rare 4-mod once geared.
Sell: trade away maps whose mods your build hates - someone else can use them.
Skip: delete or archive zero-revive corrupted maps you cannot survive yet; revisit them later.

steps.label: Check the revive count
body: Confirm how many revives the Waystone grants on the map device.
Zero-revive maps need a proven, survivable build.

steps.label: Read every modifier line
body: Compare each mod against your personal forbidden-mod list.
Watch for combinations (speed + projectiles, reflect + no regen).

steps.label: Confirm your defences
body: Resistances capped, flask sustain online, escape tool slotted.
If a mod removes your sustain, swap it or skip the map.

sections.title: Death diagnostic: boss or mod?
sections.intro: Died and not sure why? Pick the pattern.

rules.title: A recovery mod is silencing you
steps: No Regeneration / Reduced Recovery removes flask and skill healing.
Check for a leech-suppression mod if you rely on leech.
Run life-on-hit or skip these maps.

rules.title: A multiplier mod scaled a boss hit
steps: Increased monster damage or critical modifiers can one-shot under-geared builds.
This is the map mod, not necessarily the boss mechanic.
Cap resistances and add layered defence before re-running.

rules.title: Speed / teleport mod overwhelmed you
steps: Increased Monster Speed or teleport closes gaps fast.
Bring movement skills and clear from a defensible position.
Avoid these mods on slow, stationary builds.

rules.title: A specific modifier was the cause
steps: Identify the exact mod that broke your build.
Add it to your forbidden-mod list permanently.
Reroll, sell or skip similar maps going forward.

defaultResult.title: General death recovery
steps: Re-read the modifier line and your revive count.
Separate boss mechanics from map modifiers.
Adjust defences or skip the map.

sections.title: Community questions, answered
sections.intro: Common Waystone questions from Reddit and video comments, each with our analysis and a direct suggestion.

cards.title: Why do high-reward maps keep killing me?
body: Question: the map looked profitable but I died repeatedly.
Evidence: more modifiers means fewer revives and more danger, not just more loot.
Suggestion: run Rare 4-mod, not corrupted 6-mod, until you survive T15.

cards.title: Should I always Alchemy and Go?
body: Question: is Rare 4-mod always the play?
Evidence: it is the safe middle ground for geared builds.
Suggestion: yes for farming; skip corrupted maps you cannot survive.

cards.title: My build feels fine but a mod deletes it
body: Question: sudden deaths on specific maps.
Evidence: reflect / no-leech / no-regen target specific builds.
Suggestion: keep a personal forbidden-mod list and check it every map.

cards.title: Are Tablet mods separate from Waystone mods?
body: Question: do Tablets stack dangerously?
Evidence: Tablets add region bonuses on top of the Waystone line.
Suggestion: account for both when judging a map's danger.

entries.takeaway: Use Normal/Magic for progression and Rare 4-mod for farming; only run zero-revive corrupted maps once you survive T15.

sections.title: Troubleshooting
paragraphs: Most 'bad map' deaths are predictable once you read the line. The two failure modes are: your build lacks the defence a mod removes (regen, leech, resistances), or the mod count stripped your revives and a single mistake ended the run.
bullets: If you cannot name why you died, re-read the modifier line and the revive count.
Separate boss mechanics from map modifiers before blaming the boss.
Keep a written forbidden-mod list and check it every map open.
